options.combinedScience: Two GCSEs (grades e.g. 6-6) covering all three sciences at reduced depth
options.separateSciences: Three GCSEs (Biology, Chemistry, Physics) at greater depth

topics: Cell biology: cell structure, transport (diffusion, osmosis, active transport), cell division
Organisation: digestive system, blood and circulatory system, health and disease
Infection and response: communicable diseases, immune response, vaccination, drugs
Bioenergetics: photosynthesis, aerobic/anaerobic respiration
Homeostasis: nervous system, hormonal system, reproduction
Inheritance: DNA, RNA, protein synthesis, genetic diagrams, evolution, classification
Ecology: ecosystems, food chains, nutrient cycles, biodiversity
Atomic structure and the periodic table
Bonding, structure and properties of matter
Quantitative chemistry: moles, concentration, yield
Chemical changes: reactivity series, electrolysis, acids and bases
Energy changes: exothermic/endothermic, bond energies
Rate of reaction and equilibrium
Organic chemistry: crude oil, polymers, alcohols, carboxylic acids
Chemical analysis: chromatography, flame tests, gas tests
Chemistry of the atmosphere and using resources
Energy: stores, transfers, power, efficiency, renewable/non-renewable sources
Electricity: current, voltage, resistance, domestic circuits, static, mains supply
Particle model of matter: states, changes of state, gas pressure and temperature
Atomic structure: atomic model, radioactivity, nuclear equations, half-life, uses
Forces: contact/non-contact, pressure, Newton's laws, momentum, stopping distances
Waves: wave properties, electromagnetic spectrum, sound, light, lenses
Magnetism: magnets, electromagnetism, motors, transformers

examStructure: Combined Science: 6 papers (2 bio, 2 chem, 2 phys), each 1h15m. Separate Sciences: 2 papers per subject, each 1h45m.
